title: Force and motion - 123 school
heading: Force and motion
intro: Test your knowledge by typing your answer and comparing it with the correct answer. Then click 'Check answers'.
All the data you need is in the question. Round to the correct number of digits.

questions.q: What is the SI unit of speed?
Convert 20 m/s to km/h.
Convert 54 km/h to m/s.
Which formula applies to speed when the speed is constant?
A cyclist travels at 5.0 m/s. How far does he get in 12 s?
A runner runs 150 m at a speed of 6.0 m/s. How long does it take?
A walker covers 3.0 km in 20 minutes. What is his average speed in km/h?
A car travels 60 km in 1.0 hour and then 100 km in 1.0 hour. What is the average speed?
What do you see in a (s,t) graph with a horizontal line?
What does a straight, sloping upward line in a (s,t) graph mean?
What does a horizontal line in a (v,t) graph mean?
What does a straight, sloping upward line in a (v,t) graph mean?
How do you find the distance travelled from a (v,t) graph?
questions.a: From the area under the graph

questions.q: In a (v,t) graph the speed is constant at 10 m/s for 6.0 s. How far does the object travel?
What is the SI unit of acceleration?
A car accelerates from 0 to 20 m/s in 8.0 s. What is the average acceleration?
A car brakes from 25 m/s to a standstill in 5.0 s. What is the deceleration?
A 1200 kg car accelerates at 2.0 m/s<sup>2</sup>. What is the resultant force?
A resultant force of 300 N gives an object an acceleration of 1.5 m/s<sup>2</sup>. What is the mass?
A resultant force of 50 N acts on a 10 kg cart. What is the acceleration?
What happens to an object when the resultant force is 0 N?
questions.a: It stays at rest or moves at constant speed

questions.q: The driving force of a car is 500 N and the friction force is also 500 N. What kind of motion does the car make?
The driving force is 800 N and the friction force is 300 N. What is the resultant force?
questions.a: F<sub>res</sub> = 800 − 300 = 500 N in the direction of travel; the car accelerates

questions.q: What does Newton's third law (action and reaction) state?
questions.a: Two objects exert forces of equal size and opposite direction on each other

questions.q: You push a crate 5.0 m forward with a force of 40 N. How much work do you do? (W = F × s)
Lifting an object over 6.0 m takes 300 J of work. What is the force?
A driver travels at 20 m/s and has a reaction time of 0.75 s. What is the reaction distance?
The reaction distance is 14 m and the braking distance is 26 m. What is the stopping distance?
questions.a: stopping distance = reaction distance + braking distance = 14 + 26 = 40 m

questions.q: A car travels twice as fast. What happens to the braking distance?
questions.a: The braking distance becomes about 4 times as large

questions.q: A stone falls without air resistance. The acceleration of free fall is 9.8 m/s<sup>2</sup>. What is the speed after 2.0 s?
A parachutist descends at constant speed. Which statement is correct?
questions.a: The force of gravity is equal to the air resistance

questions.q: Why do you slide forward when a car suddenly brakes?
questions.a: Because of inertia you keep moving at the same speed

questions.q: Why does a crumple zone reduce the force on the occupants in a collision?
questions.a: The car slows down over a longer time, so the deceleration is smaller

questions.q: Which two parts make up the stopping distance?
How do you find the speed from a (s,t) graph?
questions.a: From the slope of the line: v = Δs / Δt
